subject: Barricade (pews and rubble)

source_quote: Bugbears behind an improvised barricade of pews and rubble...

subject: black stone steps
fact: The broad steps of dull black stone descend from the north wall into shadow, serving as a physical pathway toward deeper, unknown regions of the ruin.
source_quote: Broad steps of dull black stone descended from the north wall into shadow.

subject: Blessed Plate Mail
fact: Calmer’s blessed plate mail, the finest protection available to a cleric of his station, was pierced by the wraith’s touch and then compounded by a stray fire bolt — proving even superior magical armor cannot guarantee survival against supernatural malice.

subject: Captain Tolub's ship schedule
fact: Captain Tolub's ship schedule is a tracked logistical detail that Zephyr maintains in his mental ledger of obligations and future actions.
source_quote: He filed the directions away in the same place he kept everything he planned to collect later: the Rhennee debt, Captain Tolub's ship schedule, the exact weight of every favor he was owed.

subject: Dagger
fact: Zephyr carries a dagger, drawn in anticipation of ghoul attack, as part of his prepared response to paralysis-inducing undead.
source_quote: The dagger was already in my hand.

subject: Dropped Ghoul
fact: The dropped ghoul — killed by Sequoia’s arrow before it could act — is a physical artifact of necromantic interference, bearing the insignia of the Earth Temple and demonstrating the precision of its reanimation and deployment.
source_quote: I looked at the dropped ghoul — my ghoul, killed before it could act, the assassin's precision Zinnia respects and won't say he respects — and then at the door where the others had fled.

subject: Iron Shackles
fact: The iron shackles are heavy, rusted restraints designed to immobilize and degrade. They opened cleanly under precise lockpicking, suggesting they were poorly maintained or intentionally weakened — perhaps by prior escape attempts.
source_quote: The shackles came apart like they'd been waiting for me.

subject: leash

source_quote: The leash attached to it was also real

subject: lock
fact: The lock on the prisoner's shackles gave cleanly when picked.
source_quote: I stepped forward, crouched down, and got to work. The lock gave cleanly.

subject: Map with Hidden Passage Marked
fact: The map, annotated by the freed prisoner, contains a precise notation of the hidden passage into the Deep Temple. Its accuracy is confirmed by Zephyr’s mental verification, making it a critical tactical asset.
source_quote: He pointed it out on our map. Precise.

subject: Pistol
fact: Zephyr’s pistol is the only weapon to land a tangible wound on the wraith, though the damage was negligible.
source_quote: Zephyr raised his pistol. The shot caught the wraith across what might generously be called its torso — a wound that barely registered...

subject: Plate Mail
fact: The cleric wears blessed and magical plate mail, considered the finest protection available to a cleric of their station, which failed to prevent the wraith’s strike.
source_quote: plate mail, blessed and magical, the finest protection available to a cleric of my station and general level of being-placed-in-danger-repeatedly.

subject: Shackles
fact: The shackles are iron restraints used to imprison temple dissidents; they were picked cleanly by Zinnia, demonstrating her mastery of mechanical systems and reinforcing her role as an enabler of freedom.

source_quote: The shackles came apart like they'd been waiting for me.

subject: tapestry

source_quote: The tapestries showed raiding — figures in the act of taking, burning, dragging.

subject: The Map
fact: The map is a physical artifact used by the party to navigate the temple; it was annotated by the freed prisoner with the precise location of the hidden passage, turning it from a tool into a key.

subject: The Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is a summoned or controlled artifact that responds to Hartsch’s whistle, implying it is bound by an arrangement that makes it act as an extension of his will.
source_quote: Because Hartsch whistled and the Obsidian Edge came running, because that was the arrangement they had made.

subject: The Rhennee debt
fact: The Rhennee debt is a recorded obligation that Zephyr keeps mentally cataloged alongside other debts, favors, and schedules as part of his personal accounting.
source_quote: He filed the directions away in the same place he kept everything he planned to collect later: the Rhennee debt, Captain Tolub's ship schedule, the exact weight of every favor he was owed.

subject: trophies on the walls
fact: The trophies — mummified heads, torn battle standards, battered shields, and a broken broadsword — are relics of conquest, preserved as symbols of dominance.
source_quote: mummified heads, their leather-dry mouths still twisted in the expressions of their dying moments. Torn battle standards. Battered shields. A broken broadsword that someone had kept as a trophy.

subject: trophies value
fact: The trophies on the walls include mummified heads, torn battle standards, battered shields, and a broken broadsword, but no monetary value is stated.
source_quote: The trophies on the walls said as much: mummified heads... Torn battle standards. Battered shields. A broken broadsword...

subject: Zephyr’s Dagger
fact: Zephyr’s dagger was used to execute a flawless, pre-emptive kill on the first ghoul — a strike so precise it prevented the creature from even initiating its attack, embodying the assassin’s principle of eliminating threats before they become threats.

subject: alliance with Hartsch

subject: Calmer's Identity
fact: There is an unresolved thread concerning whether Calmer’s recent divine outbursts and vocal mania are the result of his own faith intensifying under pressure — or whether he is being overwritten by an external, possibly infernal or celestial, entity using his body and voice as a vessel.
source_quote: The second thought was quieter and I didn't linger on it. The second thought was: *is that him, or is that something else wearing his voice?*

subject: Calmer’s Transformation
fact: Calmer’s two failed attempts against the wraith were followed by an explosive, almost ecstatic release of divine power against ghouls — raising concerns among allies that his faith may be corrupted, his psyche fractured, or his body inhabited by something that uses his voice and power.

subject: Calmer's transformation
fact: Zephyr suspects Calmer's rage against undead may be something more than mere faith — possibly a change in his core identity.
source_quote: is that him, or is that something else wearing his voice?

subject: Fate of the Four Remaining Prisoners
fact: Four captives remain chained in the dungeon. Their release is pending, and their potential knowledge or loyalty is unassessed. Their survival may hinge on whether the party has time, resources, or will to free them before moving on.
source_quote: The other four were still chained to the wall. I had more work to do.

subject: favors owed
fact: Zephyr filed the exact weight of every favor he was owed among the things he planned to collect later.
source_quote: He filed the directions away in the same place he kept everything he planned to collect later: the Rhennee debt, Captain Tolub's ship schedule, the exact weight of every favor he was owed.

subject: Kelno's Endgame
fact: Kelno’s silent manipulation of the temple war raises the question of what his true objective is — whether he seeks to claim the dungeon for himself, to resurrect a lost power, or to eliminate all rivals and emerge as the sole surviving temple authority.
source_quote: Kelno had read the board and decided his move was to let the other temples destroy each other while his people walked the corridors with empty bags and filled them.

subject: Kelno’s Role and Knowledge
fact: Kelno is an unnamed insider who possessed knowledge of the Deep Temple’s hidden passage. His connection to the prisoner suggests he is a key figure in the Air Temple’s resistance network — his whereabouts and current status are unknown.
source_quote: knowledge he'd gotten directly from Kelno — which meant it was the kind of information that doesn't circulate widely, the kind you only know if you were close enough to matter or close enough to overhear.

subject: Kelno’s True Intent
fact: Kelno’s quiet manipulation of the war suggests he is not merely a survivor but a master strategist; his next move — and whether he intends to ally with or betray the Obsidian Edge — remains unknown.

subject: language barrier with elementals
fact: The elemental combatants communicate in Primordial, a language none of the party speaks, creating an unbridgeable gap to potential intelligence about the deep temple.
source_quote: They were not men. They were elemental things, and whatever they spoke was Primordial — a tongue none of us carried.

subject: Necromancer's Identity
fact: The identity and allegiance of the necromancer raising Earth Temple corpses remains unknown — whether they are a rogue agent, a traitor within the temples, or an external force exploiting the war to rebuild an undead army.
source_quote: Someone with necromantic power was working in this dungeon right now, during our carefully engineered war, with access to our people's corpses and apparent interest in deploying them.

subject: Necromantic Interference
fact: The raising of Earth Temple members as ghouls implies an unseen necromancer operating within the temple war, violating established battlefronts and tactics.
source_quote: now raised by something with necromantic ambitions and sent wandering down here to scavenge whatever the temple war left behind.

subject: Necromantic Interference
fact: The resurrection and deployment of Earth Temple members as ghouls during the temple war suggests an unseen necromancer is manipulating both factions — possibly to exploit the chaos, harvest souls, or eliminate key players — with access to corpses and intimate knowledge of the party’s operations.

subject: necromantic presence

source_quote: Someone with necromantic power was working in this dungeon right now, during our carefully engineered war, with access to our people's corpses and apparent interest in deploying them.

subject: prisoners' fate

source_quote: "Please, please don't leave us to die!"

subject: self-determination
fact: The individual is choosing his path deliberately, asserting autonomy despite being part of a controlled alliance.
source_quote: The kind of man who goes where he chooses, and who happens to be choosing this

subject: Steam Phenomenon
fact: An unexplained, escalating steam phenomenon persists after the battle, feeding on elemental violence and threatening to become indiscriminate.
source_quote: The steam was still there, and it was getting worse. Elemental violence has a way of feeding itself...

subject: The Deep Temple’s Nature
fact: The Deep Temple is not a destination but a threshold; it is feared, avoided, and shrouded in silence — its true purpose, occupants, and power remain hidden behind language, fear, and locked doors.

subject: the door's surveillance
fact: The self-moving door implies an unseen observer tracking the party’s movements, with intent unknown — asset or threat, TBD.
source_quote: Someone, or something, was tracking our position. ... Still watching us, or already forgotten? I didn't know.

subject: the door that moves on its own
fact: A door that moves on its own in the Hall of Trophies is being watched by someone or something.
source_quote: Someone, or something, was tracking our position.

subject: The Moving Door
fact: A door in the Hall of Trophies opened and closed on its own during the elemental battle; it was not a draft or mechanism but likely an observer — an unknown entity tracking the party’s movements.

subject: the prisoner's mother
fact: The freed prisoner's mother raised him not to be a fool.
source_quote: My mother never raised — didn't raise me to be a fool.

subject: the Rhennee debt
fact: Zephyr filed the Rhennee debt among the things he planned to collect later.
source_quote: He filed the directions away in the same place he kept everything he planned to collect later: the Rhennee debt, Captain Tolub's ship schedule, the exact weight of every favor he was owed.

subject: The Runner’s Urgency
fact: The Earth Temple runner’s immediate summons implies the Obsidian Edge is accelerating its plans; the party’s delay in reaching the Deep Temple may now conflict with a larger, unfolding agenda.

subject: The Source of the Steam
fact: The steam filling the corridor is not natural — it is intensifying, feeding on elemental violence, and appears to be generated by an unknown force that persists despite the battle’s outcome — suggesting the temple’s magical infrastructure is failing or being actively corrupted.

subject: The Wraith’s Intent
fact: The wraith did not merely attack — it announced its intent to kill one of the party, laughed hysterically after wounding Calmer, and resisted divine power with calm superiority — suggesting it is not a random undead, but a deliberate agent with a personal stake in the party’s destruction.

subject: This again
fact: The recurring indignity of being treated as someone else’s asset while trying to build personal autonomy is a persistent, unspoken emotional thread that haunts Zephyr’s experience.
source_quote: *This again.* Not prejudice this time. Something else. The particular indignity of being someone else's asset while you were trying to build your own balance sheet.

subject: Wraith Resilience
fact: The wraith’s immunity to holy light suggests an entity beyond conventional undead, raising questions about its origin and nature.
source_quote: The holy light dissolved into the cold air like breath in winter, leaving exactly nothing behind.

subject: Wraith’s Laughter
fact: The wraith’s hysterical laughter after the cleric’s escape is an unexplained supernatural taunt, suggesting the creature has intelligence beyond mere hunger.
source_quote: came the sound of the wraith laughing at me. *Hysterically.* It laughed at me *hysterically.*
